summary: N. S. Ramachandra Murthy worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an Epigraphy Assistant in the Andhra Pradesh Department of Archaeology and Museums and retired as Professor of Indian History and Archaeology at Sri Venkateswara University.

N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya (1928–2017) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Vice Chancellor of the National Sanskrit University from 1989 to 1994 and as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry from around 1994 to 2017.
N. Taher is an archaeologist who succeeded K. K. Muhammed as head of the Archaeological Survey of India's Bhopal circle.

N. Veezhinathan, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, earned his PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964, supervised by A. Sankaran. After working at Deccan College (1960–1963), he became Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1964.

N. Venkataramanayya (1891–1976) studied under Ferrand E. Corley in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Reader in Indian History at the University of Madras (attested 1957) and Deputy Director for Epigraphy in Andhra Pradesh.

Nadine Stchoupak (1886–1941) studied at Saint Petersburg State University and EPHE under Oldenburg, Foucher, Lévi, Finot, and Meillet. Working in Indology and linguistics, she taught Sanskrit at EPHE (1931–1937) and was secretary-librarian at the Institut de Civilisation Indienne (1927–1939).

Nae Ionescu (1890–1940) was a Romanian scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Bucharest, University of Göttingen, and University of Munich, and later taught at the University of Bucharest from circa 1919 to 1938.
Nagin J. Shah (born 1931) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. Succeeding Dalsukh Malvania, he served as Acting Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology from circa 1968 to 1991.

Nalinaksha Dutt (1894–1973), an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and University of London. He headed Calcutta's Department of Pali (ca. 1924–1958) and served as President of The Asiatic Society (1959–1961).

Nalini Balbir (born 1955) studied under Colette Caillat in Indology and linguistics. She served at CNRS (1982–1988), became Professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1988, and was Directeur d'Études for Middle-Indian Philology at EPHE from 2000, becoming Emerita in 2022.
Nalini Devdas is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. She earned a PhD from Concordia University (attested 2004) under Leslie Orr and held a post at Carleton University.

Nam-lin Hur, a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and history, studied at the University of Tokyo and completed a doctorate under Helen Hardacre. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard and became a professor at the University of British Columbia (attested 2000).

Naman P. Ahuja (born 1974) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at SOAS University of London and serves as Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

Namgyal Rinpoche (1931–2003) studied at Jarvis Baptist Seminary and the University of Michigan before receiving traditional Buddhist training under Sayadaw U Thila Wunta, Mahasi Sayadaw, Phra Rajasiddhimuni, and the 16th Karmapa. He founded Kagyu Samye Ling and the Dharma Centre of Canada.

Namio Egami (1906–2002) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930) and later taught there (~1949–1967). A scholar of archaeology, history, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he served as Director of the Ancient Orient Museum (~1978–2002).
Namita Das is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned her PhD at Gauhati University under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma.

Namkhai Norbu (1938–2018), a Tibetan Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Derge Gonchen, Kuse Serjong Shedra, and Khamdre Shedra under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö. He was a professor at the University of Naples from 1962/1964 to 1992.

Nancy E. Levine (born 1949) is a scholar of Tibetology and anthropology. She has held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, serving as Associate Professor (attested 1998) and Professor of Anthropology (attested 2026).

Nancy G. Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied at Bryn Mawr, Columbia, UC Berkeley, and the University of Chicago. She has held posts at Lawrence University and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

Nancy Hatch Dupree (1927–2017) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She studied at Barnard College (~1945–1949) and Columbia University (~1950–1952), and later held a post at Kabul University (~2006–2017).
